WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Dhubri in his Supplementary Report, received through the CEO, 
Assam vide his letter no. ELE.64/2023/Vol-I/19, dated 20.09.2025 has reported that Sh. Alakesh Roy has not 
submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. 
Alakesh Roy has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India for failure to 
lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Alakesh Roy has 
failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Alakesh Roy, resident of Vill- Uttar Raipur Pt.II, P.O. 
Moterjhar, P.S. Golakganj, Dist. Dhubri, Assam, Pin-783334 and a contesting candidate from 02- Dhubri 
Parliamentary Constituency of state of Assam, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either 
House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a 
period of three years from the date of this order.

आयोग को अपना अभ्यावेदन लिखित रूप में प्रस्तुत करने और नोटिस के प्राप्त होने की तारीख से 20 दिनों के भीतर जिला

यत:, मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी, असम से उनके दिनांक 20.09.2025 के पत्र सं. 5/ 5.64/2023/४0-॥19, के

निर्वाचन व्यय के लेखे का कोई विवरण प्रस्तुत नहीं किया है। इसके अतिरिक्त, उक्त नोटिस मिलने के उपरांत,

आयोग को न तो कोई कारण बताया है और न ही कोई स्पष्टीकरण दिया है; और 


यत:, लोक प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1951 की धारा 10क में यह उपबंधित किया गया है कि:- 
“यदि निवाचिित आयोग का सयाधान हो जाता है कि कोई व्यक्ति-

है, दाखिल करने यें असफल CET है; तथा 
(व) उस असफलता के लिए कोई अच्छा कारण या न्यायोचित्य नहीं रखता है;

यत:, तथ्यों और उपलब्ध रिकार्डों के आधार पर, आयोग का यह समाधान हो गया है कि सुश्री राधारानी विश्वास 
अपने निर्वाचन व्यय के लेखे दाखिल करने में असफल रही हैं और उनके पास ऐसा करने में असफल रहने के लिए कोई भी 
उचित कारण अथवा औचित्य नहीं है; और

76/AS-LS/02/2024/CEMS-I, dated 307 December, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Ms. Radharani Biswas, for not lodging of the account 
of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Ms. Radharani Biswas was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission

WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:-

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 20th November, 2025 


O.N. 19.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Punjab, 2024, for 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary 
Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/EPS/2024(7), 
dated 77 May, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary Constituency of Punjab, 2024 was 
declared by the Returning Officer on 04" June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 05.07.2024 of DEO, Ludhiana under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2024/R-7458, dated 
22.07.2024 stating that Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran, a contesting candidate from 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary 
Constituency of state of Punjab has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 76/PB- 
LS/07/2024/CEMS-I, dated 06" February, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections 
Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran, for not lodging of the account 
of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran was directed to submit representation in writing to the 
Commission explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses 
with the District Election Officer, Ludhiana District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the DEO, Ludhiana has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Sh. Amritpal 
Singh Chhandran on 13.02.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Ludhiana in his Supplementary Report, received through the CEO, 
Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2025/R-1601, dated 07.04.2025 has reported that Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran has 
not submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, 
Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of 
India for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Amritpal Singh 
Chhandran has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the 
failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran, resident of H.No. 613, Azad Nagar, 
Patiala, Punjab, Pin-147001 and a contesting candidate from 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary Constituency of State of 
Punjab, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the 
Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date 
of this order.

Parliamentary Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No.

WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and

WHEREAS, the result of the election for 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary Constituency of Punjab, 2024 was

Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 04.07.2024 of DEO, Ludhiana under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2024/R-7458, dated 
22.07.2024 stating that Sh. Ravinder Pal Singh Baba Ji Barger Wala, a contesting candidate from 07- Ludhiana 
Parliamentary Constituency of state of Punjab has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required 
under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 76/PB- 
LS/07/2024/CEMS-I, dated 06" February, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections 
Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Ravinder Pal Singh Baba Ji Barger Wala, for not lodging 
of the account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Ravinder Pal Singh Baba Ji Barger Wala was directed to submit representation in 
writing to the Commission explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his 
election expenses with the District Election Officer, Ludhiana District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the 
notice; and 


WHEREAS, the DEO, Ludhiana has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Sh. Ravinder 
Pal Singh Baba Ji Barger Wala on 11.02.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Ludhiana in his Supplementary Report, received through the CEO, 
Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2025/R-1601, dated 07.04.2025 has reported that Sh. Ravinder Pal Singh Baba Ji 
Barger Wala has not submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt 
of the said notice, Sh. Ravinder Pal Singh Baba Ji Barger Wala has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to 
the Election Commission of India for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; 
and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Ravinder Pal 
Singh Baba Ji Barger Wala has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or 
justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Ravinder Pal Singh Baba Ji Barger Wala, resident of 
H.No. 1202, St. No. 10, Guru Arjan Dev Nagar, Ludhiana, Punjab, Pin-141008 and a contesting candidate from

member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union 
Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

O.N. 28.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Rajasthan, 2023 for 80-Rajakhera 
Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No.464/RJ-LA/2023, 
dated 30" October, 2023; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election

Officer an account of his election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent 
under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election from 80-Rajakhera Assembly Constituency of 
Rajasthan, 2023 was declared by the Returning Officer on 3 December, 2023 and hence the last date for lodging the 
account of Election Expenses was 2™ January, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by DEO, Dholpur report dated 11.01.2024 forwarded by the Chief 
Electoral Officer, Rajasthan vide his letter no. F.3(1)(S)EEM/ELECTION/Candidates’ Exp./433 dated 16.01.2024, 
under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Vinay Sikarvar a contesting candidate 
from 80-Rajakhera Assembly Constituency of state of Rajasthan has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as 
required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Dholpur a Show-Cause notice 
No. 76/RJ-LA/80/2023/CEMS-I, dated 28" February, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Vinay Sikarvar for not lodging of 
account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Vinay Sikarvar, was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Dholpur within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Dholpur vide his letter no. Ele./LSGE/EVM/2024/839 dated 
22.03.2024 has informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Vinay Sikarvar’s Sister (name 
Kumari Madhuri), on dated 12.03.2024; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Dholpur in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. 
37/Elec./Account/2025/120 dated 13.02.2025 has reported that Sh. Vinay Sikarvar has not submitted account of 
election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Vinay Sikarvar has neither furnished any reason nor 
explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as 
prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Vinay Sikarvar, has 
failed to lodge account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the Election 
Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Vinay Sikarvar, residence of Bothpura, Tehsil Maniya, District 
Dholpur, Rajasthan, a contesting candidate from 80-Rajakhera Assembly Constituency of Rajasthan in General 
Election to Legislative Assembly, 2023 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House 
of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of 
three years from the date of this order.

O.N. 29.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Haryana, 2024 for 73-Kosli 
Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/ECI/HAR- 
LA/2024, dated 5° September, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana, 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" October, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 77 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by DEO, Rewari forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana 
vide his letter no. 6/Elect-Exp./GELA-HR-2024/Elec-2025/2AE-692 dated 05.02.2025, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 
of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Lavinder Singh a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly 
Constituency has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Rewari a Show-Cause notice 
No. 76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 30" April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Lavinder Singh for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Lavinder Singh was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Rewari within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari vide his letter no. Elec-2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has 
informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Lavinder Singh on 20.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Elec- 
2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Lavinder Singh has not submitted account of election expenses. 
Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Lavinder Singh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the 
Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years 
from the date of the order.”’; 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(iii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 16, 2026/वैशाख 26, 1948 75 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Lavinder Singh 
has failed to lodge account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Lavinder Singh, House No. 985, Village Kanwali, District 
Rewari, Haryana, a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana in General Election to 
Legislative Assembly, 2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the 
Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three 
years from the date of this order. 


[F. No. 76/HR-LA/73/2024/CEMS-I] 
By Order, 
RAKESH KUMAR, Secy.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 27th November, 2025 


O.N. 30.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Haryana, 2024 for 73-Kosli 
Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/ECI/HAR- 
LA/2024, dated 5h September, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana, 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" October, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 77 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by DEO, Rewari forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, 
Haryana vide his letter no. 6/Elect-Exp./GELA-HR-2024/Elec-2025/2AE-692 dated 05.02.2025, under sub-rule (1) of 
Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Naval Singh a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly 
Constituency has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Rewari a Show-Cause notice 
No. 76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 30" April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Naval Singh for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and

WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Naval Singh was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Rewari within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari vide his letter no. Elec-2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has 
informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Naval Singh on 20.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Elec- 
2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Naval Singh has not submitted account of election expenses. 
Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Naval Singh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the 
Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years 
from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Naval Singh 
has failed to lodge account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Naval Singh, House No. 89, Village Mandiya Khurd, Tehsil 
and District Rewari, Haryana, a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana in 
General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of 
either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory 
for a period of three years from the date of this order.

O.N. 31.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Haryana, 2024 for 73-Kosli 
Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/ECI/HAR- 
LA/2024, dated 50 September, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana, 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" October, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 77 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by DEO, Rewari forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana 
vide his letter no. 6/Elect-Exp./GELA-HR-2024/Elec-2025/2AE-692 dated 05.02.2025, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 
of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Mukesh Kumar a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly 
Constituency has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Rewari a Show-Cause notice No. 
76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 30™ April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Mukesh Kumar for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Mukesh Kumar was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Rewari within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari vide his letter no. Elec-2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has 
informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Mukesh Kumar on 20.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Elec- 
2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Mukesh Kumar has not submitted account of election expenses. 
Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Mukesh Kumar has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the 
Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years 
from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Mukesh Kumar 
has failed to lodge account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Mukesh Kumar, VPO Mandola, District Rewari, Haryana, a 
contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana in General Election to Legislative Assembly, 
2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the 
Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date 
of this order.

after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Mukesh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election

NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Mukesh, House No. 1472, Samaypur Road, Rajeev Colony, 
Ballabgarh, District-Faridabad, Haryana-121004, a contesting candidate for 85-Prithla Assembly Constituency 
of Haryana in General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a 
member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 7th May, 2025 


O.N. 36.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of West Bengal, 2024 for 08-Maldaha Dakshin 
Parliamentary Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 
464/EPS/2024(3) dated 12nd April, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer, an account of his election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent 
under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned elections for 08-Maldaha Dakshin Parliamentary 
Constituency of West Bengal, was declared by the Returning Officer on 47 June, 2024 and hence the last date for 
lodging the account of Election Expenses was 47 July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Malda report dated 05.07.2024 
forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal vide his letter no. 4552-Home (Elec.) dated 197 July, 2024, 
under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan, a contesting 
candidate from 08-Maldaha Dakshin Parliamentary Constituency of state of West Bengal, has failed to lodge 
account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said reports of the District Election Officer, Malda a Show-Cause notice No. 
76/WB/PC-08/2024/CEMS-IV dated 177 September, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 
of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan, for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan, was directed to submit his representation in writing to the 
Commission explaining the reason for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the 
District Election Officer, Malda within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Malda vide his letter No. 945/VIII-9/Elec dated 24" December, 
2024 it has informed that the notice was served to Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan on 297 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Malda in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. 945/VIII- 
9/Elec dated 247 December, 2024 has reported that Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan has not submitted account of 
election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan has neither furnished any 
reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account as prescribed under law; 
and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three 
years from the date of the order.” 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Ahmed Hedatul 
Hasan, has failed to lodge his account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to 
do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan resident of Vill- Hoglabari, P.O. - 
Kankuria, Dist - Murshidabad, West Bengal, Pin - 742202, a contesting candidate in 08-Maldaha Dakshin 
Parliamentary Constituency of General Election to the Lok Sabha of West Bengal, 2024 to be disqualified for 
being chosen as and for being a member of either House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or Legislative 
Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

Sahani, a contesting candidate from 06-Balurghat Parliamentary Constituency of state of West Bengal, has failed

O.N. 39.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2021 for 93-Pala Assembly

WHEREAS, as per the Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate 
at an election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election

under Section 77 of the said act; and 

WHEREAS, the result of the election for 93-Pala Assembly Constituency was declared by the Returning 
Officer on 02" May, 2021 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election Expenses was 01“ June, 2021; 
and 


WHEREAS, the Commission having regard to the then prevailing pandemic situation of Covid-19, decided to 
condone any incidence of late submission of the account by candidate till 317 July, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report of the District Election Officer, Kottayam, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his letter no. EL1/2/2021- 
ELEC; dated 02.11.2022 stating that Sh. Albin Mathew, a contesting candidate from 93-Pala Assembly 
Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the Legislative Assembly, 2021 has failed to lodge his account of 
election expenses, as required under law; and 

WHEREAS, on basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Kottayam a ‘Show Cause Notice’ No. 
76/KL-LA/93/2021/CEMS-II, dated 09" February, 2023 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Albin Mathew, for not lodging the account of

reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election 
expenditure as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: -

(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this

the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’;

has failed to lodge his account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of the Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the

New Delhi, the 12th August, 2025 


O.N. 40.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2021 for 96-Ettumanoor Assembly 
Constituency of Kerala was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/KL- 
LA/2021, dated [20 March, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, as per the Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate 
at an election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent 
under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 96-Ettumanoor Assembly Constituency was declared by the 
Returning Officer on 02" May, 2021 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election Expenses was 
017 June, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, the Commission having regard to the then prevailing pandemic situation of Covid-19, decided to 
condone any incidence of late submission of the account by candidate till 317 July, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report of the District Election Officer, Kottayam, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his letter no. EL1/2/2021- 
ELEC; dated 24.08.2021 stating that Sh. Charley Thomas Panickaridam, a contesting candidate from 96- 
Ettumanoor Assembly Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the Legislative Assembly, 2021 has failed to 
lodge his account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Kottayam a ‘Show Cause Notice’ No. 
76/KL-LA/2021/CEMS-II, dated 06" October, 2021 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Charley Thomas Panickaridam, for not lodging 
the account of Election Expenses; and 

WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Charley Thomas Panickaridam was directed to submit a representation in writing to the 
Commission explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and 
also to lodge account of election expenses with the District Election Officer, Kottayam within 20 days from the date 
of receipt of the notice; and 

WHEREAS, the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala, vide his report no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC dated 30.07.2025, has 
forwarded to the Commission the original certified copy of the notice, which was served to the aforesaid candidate on 
17.11.2021, as certified by the District Election Officer, Kottayam; 

WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Kottayam in his Supplementary Report dated 29.07.2025 as 
forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his letter no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC; dated 30.07.2025 on account 
of the candidate, has reported that Sh. Charley Thomas Panickaridam has not submitted any representation or 
statement of correct account of election expenses. Besides, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Charley Thomas 
Panickaridam has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to 
lodge the account of his election expenditure as prescribed under law; and 

WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 

“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(c) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 

(d) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 

the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 

person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’; 

WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Charley 
Thomas Panickaridam has failed to lodge his account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification 
for the failure to do so; and 

NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of the Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Charley Thomas Panickaridam, resident of — Panikkaridam 
House, Arppookkara East P O, Kottayam District and a contesting candidate from 96-Ettumanoor Assembly 
Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the Legislative Assembly, 2021, to be disqualified for being chosen as 
and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a 
State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

Returning Officer on 027 May, 2021 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election Expenses was 01“ 
June, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, the Commission having regard to the then prevailing pandemic situation of Covid-19, decided to 
condone any incidence of late submission of the account by candidate till 317 July, 2021; and

WHEREAS, as per the report dated 30.09.2022 of the District Election Officer, Kottayam, under sub-rule (1) 
of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his 
letter no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC; dated 02.11.2022 stating that Sh. Arun Mangattu, a contesting candidate from 97- 
Kottayam Assembly Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the Legislative Assembly, 2021 has failed to

Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Arun Mangattu., for not lodging the account of 
Election Expenses in the manner; and 

WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Arun Mangattu was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account in the manner and also to submit the requisite vouchers of election 
expenses with the District Election Officer, Kottayam within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 

WHEREAS, the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala, vide its letter no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC; dated 03.11.2023, has 
forwarded the original acknowledgement of the ‘Show Cause Notice’ served to Sh. Arun Mangattu on 09.03.2023; 
and

, 


person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’;

O.N. 49.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 
2025 for 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification 
No. 464/ECI/DL-LA/2025, dated 10" January, 2025; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election Officer 
an account of his election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent under 
Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency of National Capital Territory of 
Delhi, 2025 was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" February, 2025 and hence the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 10" March, 2025; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 11.03.2025 of DEO, New Delhi under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 
of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi vide his letter No. 
CEO/COE/102(121)/2024/1637 dated 26.03.2025, Sh. Haidar Ali, a contesting candidate from 40-New Delhi Assembly 
Constituency of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 2025 has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required 
under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 76/दिल्ली 


वि0स0/व्यय लेखा/2025/सी0ई0एम0एस0-1, dated 29" April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 


of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Haidar Ali, for not lodging of account of Election 
Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Haidar Ali, was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission explaining 
the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of election expenses with the District Election 
Officer, New Delhi, District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi, has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to 
Sh. Haidar Ali, on dated 07.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, New Delhi in his Supplementary Report dated 16.07.2025 has 
reported that Sh. Haidar Ali, has not submitted any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt 
of the said notice, Sh. Haidar Ali has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of 
India for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that :- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Haidar Ali, has 
failed to lodge account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act,1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Haidar Ali, R/o D.S. Andh Mahavidhyalaya, P.K. Road, New 
Delhi, GPO Central, Delhi-110001 and a contesting candidate from 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency in General 
Election to the Legislative Assembly of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 2025, to be disqualified for being chosen 
as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of 
a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 11th March, 2026 
O.N. 51—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of National Capital Territory of 


Delhi, 2025 for 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India 
Notification No. 464/ECI/DL-LA/2025, dated 10"J anuary, 2025; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent 
under Section 77 of the said act; and

WHEREAS, the result of the election for 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency of National Capital Territory 
of Delhi, 2025 was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" February, 2025 and hence the last date for lodging the 
account of Election Expenses was 10" March, 2025; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 11.03.2025 of DEO, New Delhi under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi vide his letter No. 
CEO/COE/102(121)/2024/1637 dated 26.03.2025, Sh. Virender, a contesting candidate from 40-New Delhi 
Assembly Constituency of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 2025 has failed to lodge account of election expenses, 
as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ 
No. 76/दिल्ली वि0स0/व्यय लेखा/2025/सी0ई0एम0एस0-1, dated 297 April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 
89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Virender, for not lodging of 


account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Virender, was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission explaining 
the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of election expenses with the District Election 
Officer, New Delhi, District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi, has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to 
Sh. Virender, on dated 07.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, New Delhi in his Supplementary Report dated 16.07.2025 has 
reported that Sh. Virender, has not submitted any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of 
the said notice, Sh. Virender has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India 
for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that :- 
“Tf the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Virender, has 
failed to lodge account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act,1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Virender, R/o A-302, Ground Floor, A-Block, Khanpur, JJ 
Colony, Dr. Ambedkar Nagar, New Delhi-110062 and a contesting candidate from 40-New Delhi Assembly 
Constituency in General Election to the Legislative Assembly of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 2025, to be 
disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly 
or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person,

Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to any person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt any 
person from the operation of this rule. 

5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary and expedient to do so, it 
may, by order and for the reasons to be recorded in writing in consultation with Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons.

to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, ex—servicemen and other special categories of persons 
in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this regard.

(i) the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Department of Food and Public Distribution, 
National Sugar Institute, Kanpur, of Physical Chemistry Professor and Physical Chemist, (Group ‘A’, Gazetted Post) 
Recruitment Rules, 2017 in so far as they relate to the post of Physical Chemistry Professor; 


(ii) the National Sugar Institute, Kanpur, Professor (Agriculture Chemistry), Assistant Professor (Agriculture 
Chemistry) and Junior Scientific Officer (Agriculture Chemistry), Recruitment Rules, 2019, in so far as they relate to 
the posts of Professor (Agriculture Chemistry) and Assistant Professor (Agriculture Chemistry); 


(iii) the National Sugar Institute, Kanpur, Professor (Biochemistry), Assistant Professor (Biochemistry), Junior 
Scientific Officer (Biochemistry) and Research Assistant (Biochemistry) Recruitment Rules, 2019, in so far as they 
relate to the posts of Professor (Biochemistry) and Assistant Professor (Biochemistry); 


(iv) the National Sugar Institute, Kanpur, Professor (Organic chemistry), Assistant Professor (Organic chemistry), 
Junior Scientific Officer (Organic Chemistry) and Research Assistant (Organic chemistry) Recruitment Rules, 2019, 
in so far as they relate to the posts of Professor (Organic Chemistry) and Assistant Professor (Organic Chemistry); 
and 


(v) the National Sugar Institute, Kanpur, Assistant Professor (Physical Chemistry) Recruitment Rules, 2020, 


except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the 
following rules to regulate the method of recruitment to the posts of Professor (Chemistry) and Assistant Professor 
(Chemistry) in the National Sugar Institute, Kanpur, Department of Food and Public Distribution under the Ministry 
of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distributions, namely: - 


1. Short title and commencement. — (1) These rules may be called the National Sugar Institute, Kanpur, Professor 
(Chemistry) and Assistant Professor (Chemistry) Group ‘A’ Posts, Recruitment Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Application. - These rules shall apply to the posts specified in column (1) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Number of posts, classification and Level in Pay Matrix. - The number of the said posts, their classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule. 


4. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating thereto shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the aforesaid Schedule. 


5. Disqualification. — No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living, or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
such person from the operation of this rule. 


6. Power to relax. -Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission, 
relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


7. Saving. -Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to be 
provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, ex-servicemen and other special categories of persons in 
accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this regard.

सं. 10-5/2025-यू.3(ए)--जबकि, राष्ट्रीय आयुर्वेद संस्थान (सम विश्वविद्यालय), जयपुर द्वारा यूजीसी (सम विश्वविद्यालय संस्थान) 
विनियम, 2023 के अनुसार माता मनसा देवी कॉम्प्लेक्स, पंचकुला, हरियाणा में ऑफ-कैंपस शुरू करने के लिए यूजीसी पोर्टल पर एक ऑनलाइन 
आवेदन प्रस्तुत किया गया था। 


2. और जबकि, यूजीसी ने दिनांक 02.01.2025 के अपने पत्र संख्या 38-2/2024 (सीपीपी-आई/डीयू) के माध्यम से सूचित किया कि 
आवेदन की स्थायी समिति के माध्यम से जांच की गई थी। समिति ने संस्था की प्रस्तुति के बाद और प्रस्तुत किए गए दस्तावेजों के आधार पर कुछ 
शर्तों के साथ राष्ट्रीय आयुर्वेद संस्थान (सम-विश्वविद्यालय), जयपुर को आशय पत्र (एलओआई) जारी करने की सिफारिश की। 


3. और आगे जबकि, मंत्रालय ने यूजीसी की सलाह पर माता मनसा देवी कॉम्प्लेक्स, पंचकूला, हरियाणा में ऑफ-कैंपस शुरू करने से 
पहले 3 वर्ष की अवधि के भीतर कुछ शर्तों को पूरा करने के लिए राष्ट्रीय आयुर्वेद संस्थान (सम विश्वविद्यालय), जयपुर को दिनांक 22.04.2025 
को आशय पत्र (एलओआई) जारी किया। 


4. और जबकि, कुलसचिव (कार्यवाहक), राष्ट्रीय आयुर्वेद संस्थान (सम विश्वविद्यालय), जयपुर ने दिनांक 07.10.2025 के 
पत्र संखया एफ.1(24)/एनआईए-पीके/आरईजी/एनआईए/2023-3890 के माध्यम से, एलओआई की शर्तों की पूर्ति के संबंध में अनुपालन रिपोर्ट 
प्रस्तुत की। इसे सत्यापन और आगे सलाह के लिए यूजीसी को भेजा गया था। इसके जवाब में, यूजीसी ने दिनांक 21.04.2026 के पत्र के माध्यम 
से सूचित किया कि अनुपालन रिपोर्ट को स्थायी समिति द्वारा स्वीकार कर लिया गया था और मामले में अंतिम अनुमोदन के लिए सिफारिश की 
गई थी। 


5. अब, इसलिए, यूजीसी अधिनियम, 1956 की धारा 3 के तहत प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, शिक्षा मंत्रालय, यूजीसी की सलाह 
पर, एतट्टारा राष्ट्रीय आयुर्वेद संस्थान (सम-विश्वविद्यालय), जयपुर को माता मनसा देवी कॉम्प्लेक्स, पंचकुला, हरियाणा में एक ऑफ-कैंपस केंद्र 
शुरू करने के लिए अनुमोदन प्रदान करता है। 

6. राष्ट्रीय आयुर्वेद संस्थान (सम-विश्वविद्यालय), जयपुर द्वारा इस मंत्रालय की पूर्व की अधिसूचनाओं में उल्लिखित अन्य सभी शर्तों के 
साथ-साथ समय-समय पर जारी विश्वविद्यालय अनुदान आयोग और अन्य सांविधिक परिषदों के नियमों/विनियमों का पालन करेगा।

MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION) 


New Delhi-01, the 12th May 2026 


No. 10-5/2025-U.3(A)—Whereas, an online application was submitted by National Institute of Ayurveda (Deemed to 
be University), Jaipur, on the UGC Portal for starting an off-campus at Mata Mansa Devi Complex, Panchkula, Haryana as per 
the UGC (Institutions deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2023. 


2. And whereas, UGC, vide its letter No. 38-2/2024 (CPP-I/DU) dated 02.01.2025, informed that the application was 
examined through its Standing Committee. The Committee, after presentation of the Institution and based on the documents 
submitted, recommended for issuance of Letter of Intent (1.01) to National Institute of Ayurveda (Deemed to be University), 
Jaipur with certain conditions. 


3. And further whereas, the Ministry, on the advice of UGC, issued Letter of Intent (Lol) dated 22.04.2025 to National 
Institute of Ayurveda (Deemed to be University), Jaipur for fulfilment of certain conditions within a period of 3 years before 
starting an off-campus at Mata Mansa Devi Complex, Panchkula, Haryana. 


4. And whereas, Registrar (i/c), National Institute of Ayurveda (Deemed to be University), Jaipur, vide letter 
No. F.1(24)/NIA-PK/Reg/NIA/2023-3890 dated 07.10.2025, submitted compliance report in respect of fulfilment of the 
conditions of the Lol. The same was forwarded to UGC for verification and further advice. In response, UGC, vide letter dated 
21.04.2026, informed that the compliance report was accepted by the Standing Committee and recommended for final approval 
in the matter. 


5. Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, the Ministry of 
Education, on the advice of UGC, hereby accords approval to National Institute of Ayurveda (Deemed to be University), Jaipur 
to start an off-campus Centre at Mata Mansa Devi Complex, Panchkula, Haryana. 


6. All other conditions mentioned in the earlier Notification(s) of this Ministry as well as the Rules / Regulations of 
UGC and other Statutory Councils, issued from time to time, shall continue to be adhered by National Institute of Ayurveda 
(Deemed to be University), Jaipur. 


PURNENDU KISHORE BANERJEE 
Joint Secretary

S.R.O. 18.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Armed Forces Medical Stores Depot Group ‘B’ Post (Senior Stores Superintendent) Recruitment 
Rules 2005; and the Ministry of Defence, Directorate General Armed Forces Medical Services, Armed Forces 
Medical Store Depot, Storekeeping Staff Group ‘C’ posts Recruitment Rules, 2006, in so far as they relate to the post 
of Store Superintendent, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President 
hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Senior Store Superintendent in 
the Directorate General Armed Forces Medical Services, Ministry of Defence, namely:- 


78 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA MAY 30, 2026/JY AISHTHA 9, 1948 [PART II—SEc. 4] 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Defence, Directorate General 
Armed Forces Medical Services, Senior Store Superintendent (Group ‘B’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2026. 
(2) 11679 shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of the said post, its classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt any 
person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission, 
relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to 
be provided for the Schedule Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex-servicemen and other 
special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this 
regard.

supersession of the Central Ground Water Board (Administrator, Central Ground Water Authority) Recruitment 
Rules, 2000, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby 
makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Administrator in Ministry of Jal Shakti, 
Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Central Ground Water Board, 
namely:- 


l. Short title and commencement. — (l) These rules may be called the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Department of 
Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Central Ground Water Board, 
(Administrator, Central Ground Water Authority) Recruitment Rules, 2026.

in the pay matrix attached thereto, shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to 
these rules.

No. LAFEAS-PS5001 1/1/2026/22-Perl Sec-RSS— In supersession of Notification No. RS/18/15/2014/06-Perl. dated 
27" January, 2023 and in terms of Section 4 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and 
Redressal) Act, 2013, the Secretary-General, Rajya Sabha is pleased to reconstitute the ‘Internal Committee’ w.e.f. 6th May, 
2026, comprising the following members— 


1. Dr. (Smt.) Subhashree Panigrahi, Joint Secretary - Presiding Officer 
2 Shri Jayanta Kumar Mallick, Director - Member-Secretary 
3, Ms. Chitra Gouri, Director - Member 

4. Smt. Anuja Pethia, Advocate - Member 


2. The tenure of the committee shall be for a period of one year i.e., up to 5th May, 2027, or until further orders, 
whichever is earlier. 


3. The Committee would be responsible for providing protection against sexual harassment of women in the Rajya 
Sabha Secretariat and redressal of complaints of sexual harassment and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. 


4. The Committee will exercise the powers conferred in accordance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at 
Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, and perform the duties and responsibilities as assigned to it 
under the said Act or as assigned by the Rajya Sabha Secretariat from time to time. In terms of the said Act and Sexual 
Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Rules, 2013, certain compliances are also required 
to be observed by the Committee. The mandate and some key responsibilities of the Internal Committee, in line with the 
provisions of the aforesaid Act and Rules, are annexed to this Notification. 


SREEJA V., Director 


ANNEXURE 
Mandate and key responsibilities of the Internal Committee (IC) 


1. Receiving Complaints: The IC is responsible for receiving complaints of sexual harassment from employees. On 
receipt of the complaint, the Committee shall send one of the copies received from the aggrieved woman to the 
respondent within a period of seven working days. [Rule 7(2)] 


il. Conciliation Report: In case of settlement, the IC shall record and forward the report to the employer. Also copies 
of the report shall be provided to both the parties (Section 10 (2&3). 


iil. Inquiry Process: Conducting a fair and timely inquiry into the complaints received, which shall be completed within 
a period of 90 days. [Section 11(4)]. 


iv. Recommendations: Submitting findings and recommendations (including interim measures) of the inquiry to the 
employer for appropriate action. (Section 12). 


v. Submission of Inquiry Report: On completion of the inquiry, the IC shall submit a report of its findings to the 
employer within a period of ten days from the date of completion of the inquiry. [Section 13(1)] 
V1. Confidentiality: Maintaining strict confidentiality throughout the process. (Section 16 & 17). 
Vii. Annual Reports: To prepare Annual Reports in the manner as prescribed under Rule 14 and submit to the employer 


in each Calendar Year (Section 21).
